title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Cambodia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Cambodia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Cambodia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: When a Cambodian citizen dies in Cambodia, families must obtain medical or police clearance, complete civil registration at the Commune or Sangkat level within 15 days, handle NSSF social security claims where insured, and address succession under the 2007 Civil Code. Because Cambodian domestic ministries publish limited English-language procedural portals online and civil-status regulations appear primarily in Khmer, this checklist combines verified statutory texts preserved in international repositories (FAOLEX, ILO NATLEX, and UNESCAP CRVS) with Cambodian government portals and accredited consular guidance [1][4][8][9].

steps.title: Immediate medical certification and police reporting
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinic death: The attending hospital or health center issues a medical death confirmation or hospital notification certificate identifying the cause of death for civil registration [8][9].
  • Death at home or sudden/unexpected death: For an expected death at home, notify the Village Chief (Me Phum) and Commune/Sangkat office promptly for local confirmation; for any sudden, accidental, or suspicious death, contact the local police (117) and emergency medical services (119) immediately so police and a provincial prosecutor can examine the scene and authorize release or post-mortem inspection [8][9][10].
  • Verify personal records early: Confirm exact Khmer and Latin-script spelling across the deceased's National ID card, Family Book (Siev Phov Krousar), and medical notice before visiting the civil registrar [8][10].

steps.title: Civil registration within 15 days and death certificates
steps.html:
• Strict 15-day reporting period: Under Cambodia's civil registration framework (historically Sub-Decree No. 103 on Civil Status and updated Law on Civil Status, Civil Status Statistics and Identification procedures tracked by UNESCAP and Cambodia's digital government reforms), a death must be declared within 15 days from the date of death [4][7][10].
  • Commune or Sangkat Civil Registrar: Present the hospital or Village Chief death confirmation, the deceased's Cambodian National ID card, Family Book or Residence Book, and the informant's ID to the civil registrar at the Commune or Sangkat Office (Sala Khum / Sala Sangkat) where the deceased permanently resided or where death occurred [4][8][10].
  • Timely issue vs. late registration: Timely registration within 15 days issues the original Official Death Certificate without fee; missing the deadline triggers extra district/provincial administrative verification, and ordering extra certified copies early simplifies later pension and property filings [4][10].

steps.title: Burial, cremation, repatriation, and consular legalization
steps.html:
• Burial and cremation practices: Families coordinate traditional religious rites, wat cremation, or burial once local Commune/Sangkat notification and police clearance (if applicable) are complete; international transport of remains or ashes requires the official Death Certificate, embalming or cremation certificate, non-infectious disease clearance, and airline/customs permits [8][9].
  • Cambodia is not an Apostille Convention party: As confirmed on the Hague Conference on Private International Law status table, Cambodia is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention [11].
  • MFAIC consular legalization chain: Any Cambodian death certificate, court order, or notarized estate document needed abroad must be translated if required, authenticated by the Legal and Consular Department of Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MFAIC) Cambodia in Phnom Penh, and then legalized by the destination country's embassy or consulate [6][8][9].

steps.title: Social security (NSSF), survivor pensions, and ID updates
steps.html:
• NSSF funeral grant and survivor pensions: Under the Law on Social Security Schemes (Royal Kram No. NS/RKM/1119/018) published on FAOLEX and tracked by Council for the Development of Cambodia (CDC), National Social Security Fund (NSSF) administers a lump-sum Funeral Allowance and monthly or lump-sum Survivor's Pensions (typically requiring qualifying contributor status such as 60 months of pension contributions, plus separate occupational-risk death benefits where work-related) [2][3][5].
  • Required claim documents: As documented in ILO social security operational guides, claimants must submit NSSF benefit claim forms, the official Death Certificate, National ID, Family Book, and relationship or funeral-expense proof within statutory NSSF notification and filing windows [2][5][12].
  • Update Family Book and close accounts: Record the death in the household Family Book at local police/commune offices, surrender the passport for cancellation, and notify banks and employers with the certified Death Certificate [8][10].

steps.title: Succession, wills, and land title administration
steps.html:
• Intestate and testamentary rules under the Civil Code: Book VIII (Succession) of the Civil Code of Cambodia (available in English on FAOLEX and supplemented by procedural rules on ILO NATLEX) establishes statutory heir classes, legally secured portions protecting a surviving spouse, children, and parents, and rules governing holographic, notarial, and secret wills [1][13].
  • Court and cadastral title transfers: Heirs must identify whether real estate holds a registered land title (hard title at the Ministry of Land Management, Urban Planning and Construction) or commune-level soft title, and seek formal inheritance confirmation or court probate orders when financial institutions or land registrars require judicial proof [1][9][13].
  • Property and cross-border clearance: Verify tax and transfer registration fees applicable to inherited property before selling or re-titling assets, and legalize any foreign-issued probate grant via Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MFAIC) Cambodia before local use [1][6].
